title: Our Stairs Grow One Step At NIGHT 🪜
premise: Our stairs have ten steps by day and eleven at night, and at two in the morning they creak ten times with nobody on them. Dad's one house rule is that everyone is upstairs by ten and nobody is on the stairs after, so one night I sit at the top with a flashlight to catch the new step.
twist: The eleventh step is a carpeted box Dad has set at the bottom of the stairs every night for eleven years, because something very tall climbs exactly ten steps each night and stops one short of my door. With the box in my room it reaches the landing, and shoved out in front of my door it stands one step short until dawn. Now we take turns setting it, and last night it sat down to wait.
world: a two-storey house's one straight staircase of honey oak and plum carpet with a landing, a round window and an amber nightlight, a hall with a mustard lamp, and a kitchen beside it
